historical_reviews.deepseek: The exact sensor read is relevant for this variant, but full SDR, Web thresholds and FPGA identity are missing. Its presence on the UART row is clear code-collision contamination, not evidence that UART is part of this test.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly excludes FPGA writes/reprogramming. This review adds device/bitstream provenance and distinguishes on-die junction temperature from nearby board temperature.
historical_reviews.duplicate_uart_variant: Row 1672 requires manual approved dongle, pinout/voltage, 115200 live BMC console and copy/paste; none of those prove FPGA temperature or thresholds.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-36 makes device identity, sensor source and expected thresholds readiness inputs; ED-38 forbids FPGA/BMC state changes and preserves logs/verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Verify the UBB FPGA's intended thermal channel, ensuring the reading belongs to the correct programmable device and sensor source, is human-readable and has specification-correct enabled thresholds across IPMI and both BMC-Web views.
original_method: The FPGA/board owner identifies the device and loaded image, defines whether the record is on-die junction or an external board probe, supplies operating limits and Web mappings, and automation collects passive complete sensor evidence for operator comparison.
manual_activity: The FPGA/board owner identifies the exact FPGA PN/revision and loaded bitstream, maps the named record to its junction or external probe, provides thermal limits and confirms the same sensor in Dashboard and Server Health. No UART connection is involved.
required_inputs: UBB FPGA vendor/device ID, board location, PN/revision and active bitstream/firmware identity
Sensor origin as FPGA on-die junction, external diode or nearby board probe
Exact SDR record/entity and Dashboard/Server Health mappings
Units, conversion/scale, tolerance, update rate, freshness and invalid/unavailable semantics
Expected range and enabled thresholds for documented clock/load/cooling/ambient state
Secret-safe OOB access, complete evidence retention and no-clear policy
FPGA thermal aborts and independent cooling/BMC recovery owner
safety_requirements: Match row 1855 and its variant, not the duplicate UART code alone
Do not attach a UART dongle or perform console copy/paste for this thermal case
Bind the sensor to the exact FPGA and identify junction versus external measurement
Record bitstream and load state because FPGA thermal limits and values depend on design activity
Retain complete SDR and enabled threshold flags; no 100-line cap
Do not reprogram FPGA, change clocks/power/fans/thresholds, reset BMC or clear logs
Stop on missing/stale/invalid reading, FPGA alarm, unsafe rise, threshold mismatch or BMC instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact row/variant, FPGA identity, bitstream and sensor source
Capture complete read-only SDR/Sensor inventory and exact TEMP_UBB_FPGA output
Parse temperature, units, state, freshness and enabled thresholds
Prepare matching Dashboard and Server Health entries
Correlate passive FPGA error, clock/load, fan, SEL and BMC health
Perform no UART, FPGA reconfiguration, control action or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve FPGA/bitstream identity and temperature-sensor source
Provide load-context operating range and enabled thresholds
Confirm both Web mappings and unavailable handling
Review evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Exact `sensor get 'TEMP_UBB_FPGA'` is relevant here, but unsafe credentials, truncated fallback and absent FPGA/Web provenance prevent acceptance. The SSH-wrapped copy on the duplicate UART row is unrelated contamination.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With secret-safe OOB access, capture full SDR and the exact FPGA record with threshold flags, identify device/bitstream and load state, and compare the same sensor and thresholds in Dashboard and Server Health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_UBB_FPGA, both Web paths and 1/1-minute estimates are preserved; duplicate UART wiring, console interaction and 20/20 minutes are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the record to a versioned FPGA and measurement source, collect passive temperature at a documented image/load state and reconcile enabled thresholds across raw and Web views.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds programmable-device provenance and protects the sensor review from a physical-UART duplicate-code collision.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Readable UART output says nothing about FPGA temperature; likewise a nearby board probe cannot be treated as FPGA junction temperature without the approved mapping.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Readback is passive, but wrong device, bitstream or sensor-source attribution can hide a junction hotspot.

project_override_considerations: Boards with multiple FPGAs or bitstream-dependent sensor availability require an explicit device/channel matrix. If the sensor is external, the specification must define its offset or relationship to junction limits.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and duplicate-UART separation audit
FPGA device/board/bitstream identity and measurement-source mapping
Exact SDR record/entity and both Web mappings
Value, units, state, freshness and enabled-threshold table
Documented FPGA load/clock/cooling/ambient context and approved limits
Complete redacted SDR plus exact sensor output with status/timestamps
Dashboard/Server Health evidence plus passive FPGA-error/fan/SEL/BMC health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1855 consistently targets an FPGA temperature sensor and Web thresholds. The BMC-UART procedure is confined to a separate duplicate-code row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive FPGA-temperature check is identifiable. Exact device, bitstream, measurement source and limits are supplyable project readiness inputs under ED-36.

review_improvement: Quarantines a physical UART duplicate, adds FPGA/bitstream and measurement-source provenance and ensures threshold/Web evidence is tied to the actual programmable device.
independent_technical_reasoning: FPGA temperature can be an on-die junction channel or an external board sensor, and the observed value depends strongly on the loaded design and activity. A name match alone cannot establish either identity or expected margin. The duplicate UART row further makes source-row binding safety-critical: physical console work must never be triggered by this passive thermal review.
